original_question: Let K be a Hilbertian field and let d >= 2. There exists a monic polynomial f(X) in K[X] of degree d and a point P in K such that the associated arboreal representation is surjective, equivalently the Odoni index iota_K(f, P) equals 1.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Conjecture 5.4 (Odoni, 1985), stated immediately after Definition 5.2 and Question 5.3(a), i.e. the polynomial/P^1 specialization of the surjective-arboreal-representation problem.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's target statement: for a Hilbertian field K and an integer d >= 2, one asks for the existence of a monic degree-d polynomial f in K[X] and a basepoint P in K such that the associated arboreal representation is surjective; it also correctly uses the equivalent Odoni-index formulation iota_K(f,P)=1.
missing_details: The statement in Section 5 inherits the standing assumption that the base field K has characteristic 0.
The arboreal representation and the Odoni index are introduced under the standing hypothesis that the inverse-image tree T_{f,∞}(P) is complete, meaning #f^{-n}(P)=d^n for every n >= 0.
A stand-alone formulation should define the arboreal representation as the Galois action rho^{arb}_{f,P}: Gal(Kbar/K) -> Aut(T_{f,∞}(P)) on the rooted tree of iterated preimages of P.
If the Odoni index notation is used, it should be defined explicitly as iota_K(f,P) = [Aut(T_{f,∞}(P)) : G_{f,∞}(P)], where G_{f,∞}(P) is the image of rho^{arb}_{f,P}.
The paper's scope here is the polynomial case on P^1/A^1; it is not the broader Question 5.3(a) for arbitrary morphisms f: P^N -> P^N or arbitrary rational functions.
To make the surjectivity claim fully precise, one should say that the image is the full automorphism group of the complete rooted d-ary preimage tree.
refined_question: Let K be a Hilbertian field of characteristic 0, and let d >= 2. Does there exist a monic polynomial f(X) in K[X] of degree d and a basepoint P in K such that the inverse-image tree T_{f,∞}(P) = {P} ⊔ f^{-1}(P) ⊔ f^{-2}(P) ⊔ ... is complete (equivalently, #f^{-n}(P)=d^n for every n >= 0) and the associated arboreal representation rho^{arb}_{f,P}: Gal(Kbar/K) -> Aut(T_{f,∞}(P)) is surjective?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: let K be a Hilbertian field of characteristic 0 and d >= 2. Does there exist a monic polynomial f(X) in K[X] of degree d and a point P in K such that T_{f,∞}(P) is complete and the Odoni index iota_K(f,P) = [Aut(T_{f,∞}(P)) : G_{f,∞}(P)] equals 1?
justification: The draft matches Conjecture 5.4 almost verbatim. The nearby paper-faithful context is essential: Section 5 begins with K of characteristic 0, defines the inverse-image tree and completeness, then defines the arboreal representation and Odoni index, and Question 5.3(a) explicitly states that iota_K(f,P)=1 is equivalent to surjectivity. Conjecture 5.4 is then the precise monic-polynomial existence statement over Hilbertian fields. So the right refinement is to add the hidden assumptions and definitions from Section 5, but not to broaden the question beyond this exact P^1/polynomial setting.
